entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Petrus Stockmans (1625-1671) was a legal advisor and professor at the University of Leiden, known for his works on Latin and Hellenistic studies. He was a prominent figure in the Dutch Golden Age, contributing to the development of the Dutch language and literature.

Stockmans' expertise in Latin and Hellenistic studies was influenced by his time at the University of Leiden, where he collaborated with prominent scholars like Johannes Meibomius and Caspar Barthius. His research on Latin and Hellenistic texts helped establish the University of Leiden as a hub for classical studies in the Netherlands.

Stockmans' legacy can be seen in the continued development of Dutch language and literature, as well as his contributions to the field of classical studies. His works on Latin and Hellenistic texts have been widely studied and continue to influence scholars today.

The 1671 edition of Stockmans' 'Liber Latinus', a collection of Latin texts, demonstrates his commitment to the study and preservation of classical literature.
